clue.text: Debussy's prelude has odd beat

indicators.note: a prelude comes at the start, so only the opening letter of the composer's name is taken

parts.note: first letter of Debussy
rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A music critic finds something strange about the rhythm in one of Debussy's piano preludes.
explanation.definitionFit: To drum is to beat repeatedly, as on a percussion instrument.

clue.text: 23 mean to eat bread regularly

indicators.note: the mean word takes the other letters into its mouth, so they go inside it

parts.note: stingy means mean, miserly

indicators.note: taking every other letter of bread at a steady interval

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of bread

explanation.surface: A miser at the table wants to eat bread only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: 23 is FISH, the answer to 23-down. 'Regularly' picks R and A from bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat cartilaginous sea creature, so it is one kind of fish.

clue.text: Teach ladies and gents to climb over church

indicators.note: the reversed toilets sit over, that is around, the church abbreviation
in a down clue, climbing means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: public toilets, loos in British English

explanation.surface: Toilet signs are shown scaling a church, an absurd picture of vandalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' and 'Gents' are British signs for public toilets, called loos.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to train or instruct them, a verb synonym of teach.

clue.text: Group of prominent scientists support writer's blocks

indicators.note: in a down clue the scientists' letters sit underneath, holding up the writer

parts.note: J. M. Barrie, author of Peter Pan
RS is the Royal Society, Britain's academy of leading scientists

explanation.surface: A panel of eminent scientists offers to help an author suffering from writer's block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's blocks' reads as a phrase, but the definition is 'blocks' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Barriers are obstacles that block passage, so the plural noun matches blocks used as a noun.

clue.text: Missing worker catches mad cow disease

indicators.note: the worker catches the disease, so its letters hold the disease's inside

parts.note: the worker ant is the standard crossword worker
BSE, bovine spongiform encephalopathy

explanation.surface: A farm hand who has not turned up for work is said to have caught mad cow disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent is not present, an adjective synonym of missing.

clue.text: Swear in debate there's no hell

indicators.note: the underworld word is absent, so those letters are removed

parts.note: to discuss is to debate
Dis is the classical underworld, hell

explanation.surface: A debate is so polite that nobody even says 'hell'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuss is an informal American-flavoured verb meaning to curse or use bad language.

clue.text: Cover for the Times entertaining the City

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest holds them inside, so the City's letters go within

parts.note: T stands for time, so two times give TT
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about The Times hosting the financial City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover a colleague or position is to guard it, so the verb is a synonym of protect.

clue.text: Bar brawl in 60 minutes or 7?

definitions.note: a cross-reference to 7-across, PROTECT; the question mark marks the verb sense

indicators.note: the jumbled bar sits within the sixty minutes

parts.note: an hour

indicators.note: a brawl is a messy fight, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A pub fight that lasts an hour, or perhaps is put down within one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to 7-across, whose answer is PROTECT, and the question mark warns that the verb sense of harbour is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour someone is to shelter or shield them, so it can stand in for guard.

clue.text: Warning soldiers after cry of surprise

indicators.note: the soldiers come after the cry, so they follow it

parts.note: O, as in 'Oh!'
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A sentry shouts a warning when soldiers appear after a startled 'Oh!'.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign of something to come, often an ominous foreboding.

clue.text: I left serious old building without perfume

indicators.note: the letters are being built up into a new arrangement
the I leaves, so it is taken out of the letter pool

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a solemn old house that has no scent at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I away from the letters of SERIOUS OLD and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odourless has no smell, the same as lacking any scent or fragrance.

clue.text: Before Sunday, no Pope destroyed books of rivals

indicators.note: everything else comes before the Sunday letter, which ends the answer
the words are wrecked, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: NT, the New Testament books

explanation.surface: Before Sunday mass, enemies of the papacy destroy holy books.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of NO POPE gives OPPONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Opponents are those on the other side in a contest, so they are competitors.

clue.text: Colour coding's initial test

indicators.note: an initial is the opening letter of a word

parts.note: first letter of coding
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A programmer's first exam involves colour-coding.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is a pinkish-orange shade named after the sea organism, so it is a hue.

clue.text: Conservative lied at first — now in trouble, the buffoon

indicators.note: only the opening letter of lied is wanted

parts.note: first letter of lied

indicators.note: a word in trouble is disturbed, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Tory politician who lied is now in trouble and looks a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A clown is a comic fool who acts silly, so a buffoon is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Standing before holy man, for example, one on retreat

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
ST, saint

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: EG, exempli gratia
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Standing before a holy man who is on a spiritual retreat, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: EG and I together give EGI, which 'on retreat' turns round to IGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige is high status or reputation in the eyes of others.

clue.text: Super important

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both enthusiastic approval and notable significance or eminence.

clue.text: Democrat party leader departing in boat

indicators.note: the first letter, the leader, goes away

parts.note: the Tory party, Britain's Conservatives

explanation.surface: A Democrat leaves on a boat while the party leader departs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dory is a small flat-bottomed rowing vessel used for fishing.

clue.text: Vehicles honked, first travelling to the rear

indicators.note: the opening letter moves from the front and ends up at the back

parts.note: in British slang honk means to smell bad, so honked is stank

explanation.surface: Cars hoot at each other in traffic, the lead driver sounding off to those behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honked' suggests a car horn, but here it is British slang for smelled bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanks are armoured military fighting machines, a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Small dalliance

definitions.meaning: second meaning: playing about, ... as a noun, as in idle flirtation

explanation.definitionFit: Trifling is both an adjective for something of little importance and a noun for flirting or toying with.

clue.text: Judge impounding European bank

indicators.note: to impound is to shut something up inside, so the European letter goes inside

parts.note: a ref, referee, judges a match

explanation.surface: A judge seizes the assets of a European bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks financial, but it is the sense of a ridge under the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or sand near the water's surface, like a sandbank.

clue.text: Demote ambassador backing heartless renegade

indicators.note: in a down clue the envoy goes underneath, backing up the other letters
with the heart removed, only the two end letters remain

parts.note: first and last letters of renegade
a legate is a papal envoy or ambassador

explanation.surface: An envoy is demoted for supporting a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate is to move someone to a lower rank, as football teams go down a division.

clue.text: Popular account: English royal abdicated over a breach

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: the shortened account is placed over, around, the A
the royal steps down and leaves, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a version is an account of events
ER, Elizabeth Regina, Queen of England

explanation.surface: A popular history of an English king's abdication and a scandal around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abdicated' takes ER out of VERSION to leave VSION, and 'over' wraps that round A to give VASION.
explanation.definitionFit: An invasion is an incursion that breaks through a border, so it is a violation of territory.

clue.text: A hairdo, say, to wear down

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; a braid is a plaited hairstyle

explanation.surface: A hairstyle, for example, that rubs away at the scalp.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to scrape or erode a surface by friction.

clue.text: Advice rejected about long division

indicators.note: the reversed advice goes about, around, the L
rejected things are sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: tips are pieces of advice

explanation.surface: A pupil refuses help with long division in maths class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long division' is a single maths phrase, but the definition is 'division' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A split is a rift or separation, a noun synonym of division.

clue.text: Australian city's extremely sorry cartoonist is sacked

indicators.note: the extremities, first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of sorry

indicators.note: sacked means fired, so the word is is thrown out of the name

parts.note: Walt Disney, the animator

explanation.surface: An Australian city's newspaper apologises after firing its cartoonist.
explanation.definitionFit: Sydney is the largest urban centre in New South Wales, Australia.

clue.text: Even Daley's twisting and turning is brought to a standstill

parts.note: par means level, equal, as in on a par

indicators.note: the letters twist and turn into a new order

explanation.surface: The diver Tom Daley twists and turns in the air before freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Daley is a British Olympic diver; 'Even' is not a letter-picking signal but PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Paralysed means unable to move or act, halted completely.

clue.text: One moving into home gets settled

indicators.note: the one letter moves into the home, going inside it

parts.note: a pad is informal for home
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A person moves into a new home and settles down.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is paid has been settled, a past-participle synonym.

clue.text: Two papers follow the Guardian's foremost talent

indicators.note: the papers follow, coming after the first letter
foremost means the very front, so the opening letter

parts.note: first letter of Guardian
the i and the FT (Financial Times) are British newspapers

explanation.surface: A boast that the Guardian leads two rival papers in talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is a natural aptitude or ability.

clue.text: Fairly loud animal?

parts.note: F is forte, loud in music
the suffix -ish means fairly, somewhat

explanation.surface: A creature that is rather noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: F-ish would mean 'fairly loud' in musical terms; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish is a creature of the water, so it is a living creature, with the question mark admitting the stretch.

clue.text: Discovery of caring female replacing male

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of the other

parts.note: minding means looking after, caring for

explanation.surface: A study finds caring women replacing men.
explanation.definitionFit: A finding is something found, as the result of an inquiry.

clue.text: Fitter of crown for the king?

definitions.text: Fitter of crown for the king?

parts.words: Fitter of crown for the king?
parts.note: reads like a royal jeweller, but the crown is a cap fitted over a tooth

explanation.surface: Who places the crown on the monarch's head at a coronation?
explanation.walkthrough: A crown is also a dental cap; anyone with a tooth, even a king, might have one fitted.
explanation.definitionFit: A tooth doctor fits artificial caps called crowns on damaged teeth.
